title: No text anywhere in the app is ever unreadable: a contrast check that fails the build
goal: User 2026-09-30: 'make sure that the text is legible. I do not want white on white or black on black cases EVER.' The history filter shipped white text on a white glass thumb (2026-09-29), and nothing caught it. Build a guard that renders the app's text-bearing controls in every state and fails on low contrast.
acceptance: Legible, as the user asked (2026-09-30: 'I didn't ask specifically for 4.5. I asked specifically for legible'): the text is plainly readable against what is actually behind it, in every state, scheme and backdrop, with no white on white or black on black ever. The system's own pairings count as legible and are kept as they are (white on the system accent, the system label colours on glass); do not darken or alter the system accent to hit a ratio. The automated check catches the real failures: text and background too close to tell apart (below about 3:1, or the same colour family on the same lightness)

A snapshot-contrast test (ImageRenderer, in Scripts/test.sh) renders every shared control that carries text or an icon (segmented control, buttons, dropdown rows, tool bar, panel rows and headers, tooltips, toasts, transport, timeline headers and clip names, the history bar, the View | Edit switch, badges, caption and title previews) in every state (rest, hover, pressed, selected, disabled, focused) and in light and dark, over white, black and mid-grey backdrops where the control is translucent or glass

For each render it measures the text or icon colour against the pixels actually behind it and fails when text or an icon is unreadable against what is behind it (below about 3:1, or same-on-same), naming the control, state, scheme and backdrop
It runs on every commit; today's offenders are listed in the task log and fixed in this task
UX-PATTERNS states the rule and points at the test

log.note: Adversarial review before building: (1) most hover states are @State inside controls and an offscreen picture has no pointer, so a shared seam (shownPointer env, answered by playtestHover and the button styles) draws hovered/pressed; (2) a white word on white leaves no trace in a picture, so each specimen is drawn three ways (shipped / words hidden by a no-op TextRenderer / words only in a flat mask colour) and the mask says where words are; (3) Liquid Glass and AppKit views do not draw offscreen (glass blanks its contents; NSViewRepresentable shows SwiftUI's yellow placeholder), so glass is stood in by white/black/grey under the kit glass tone and tooltip anchors stand aside (drawnOffscreen env); (4) a WCAG ratio alone flags white on the system accent and white on the mock's saturated clips while passing lavender on pale lavender, so the rule is 3:1, or 2:1 plainly another colour, never same family; disabled 1.8:1 = the system's disabled label.

Built: PhotonzCore Legibility + InkReading (tested, 14 tests); app DEBUG-only LegibilitySheet + LegibilityCatalogue (100 specimens, 1150 words/icons, ~12s) run by Scripts/test.sh via .build/debug/Photonz --legibility-sheet; replaces Scripts/segmented-contrast.swift. Seams: shownPointer/inkPass/drawnOffscreen env (VideoKit.swift), .measuredInk() on icons and caption bitmaps, .regularGlass(in:) for toasts. Drill: faint made #FBFCFE -> check failed at 1.00:1 naming every panel label, exit 1.

Today's offenders, all fixed: (1) caption clip name in light lavender on pale lavender 2.11:1 -> ClipKind.ink(scheme) uses the comp tone (#9A5CFF light) in ClipBar, ClipPiecesBar, CaptionCuesLayer; (2) destructive icon/pill buttons under the pointer: red on a red wash, 2.0-2.9:1 -> white on system red; (3) disabled icon/pill/caption bar buttons and picker tiles at 40-42% read 1.5-1.6:1 -> 55%; (4) faint grey on a hovered tile and on the transport glass 2.55-2.98:1 -> Palette.faint light #8B92A1 -> #7C8392; (5) mode chip chevron .tertiary 1.9:1 -> .secondary; (6) segmented chip: accent was being deepened to chase 4.5 (against the user's 10:12 correction) -> chip is the system accent, white on it, dark word only on yellow and graphite (SegmentInk.pickedWord).

Verified: Scripts/test.sh 10696/10696 plus the legibility check green; segmented-thumb-glass-walk passes with 10 real captures (history filter white on system blue legible). UX-PATTERNS: new section 'Text is always legible (a rule the build enforces)', segmented section updated. Shared controls changed, so Current gets these fixes too (task says 'anywhere in the app').

left rough, not filed (under the bar or covered here): private badges not on the sheet (CaptionGuidesOverlay badge, ColorDropNote pill, canvasNoticeChip, heldFrameBadge, HistoryOverlayCell caption) since they need EditorState/coordinator; focus rings only on the segmented control; AppKit menus/popups unmeasured (system pairings); caption preview judged against the picture without its plate (stricter than the eye).
